objective: Expand English source-domain supervision using Step-3 item-level seller-facing direct identifiers, while avoiding random easy-negative padding and product/victim-data leakage.

target_queue_size.note: This is a quality cap, not a quota. Rows must come from shared seller-facing direct identifiers.

positive: Use positive only when both sides expose the same seller-facing direct identifier, such as PGP, Telegram, Wickr, Jabber, wallet, phone, or seller-contact email.
Email or phone evidence must be treated as positive only when the snippets show seller contact context on both sides and no product/victim/sample-data cue.
A row can be appended to Step 4/5 only after explicit review; item-level extraction alone is not a label.
uncertain: Use uncertain for one-sided context weakness, generic support text, product/victim-data ambiguity, or exact identifiers embedded in sample data.
Use uncertain for same-alias or soft-same-alias continuity rows rather than primary supervision.
negative: Use negative only for clear parser noise or evidence that the shared token is not a seller identity anchor.

hard_rules: Do not use Step-7/9/11 model scores or graph membership as labels for this English expansion.
Do not label product sample credentials, victim emails, leaked-account fields, public URLs, or high-frequency generic handles as positives.
Do not pad with random easy negatives; this queue is direct-identifier positive expansion only.
After application, rerun Step 5 freeze and audit seller/alias split overlap before rerunning Linux Step 7.
